		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;text-decoration:underline;">2. Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In May 2014, the FASB</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">issued AS</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">U 2014-09, Revenue fr</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">o</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">m Contracts with Customers</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> (&#x201C;ASU 14-09&#x201D;), which</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> establish</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">es</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> a comprehensive revenue recognition standard for virtually all industries under U.S. GAAP, including those that previously followed industry-specific guidance such as the real estate, construction and software industries. The revenue standard&#x2019;s core principle is built on the contract between a vendor and a customer for the provision of goods and services. It attempts to depict the exchange of rights and obligations between the parties in the pattern of revenue recognition based on the consideration to which the vendor is entitled. To accomplish this objective, the standard requires five basic steps: i) identify the contract with the customer, (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract, (iii) determine the transaction price, (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract, and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation. The ASU is effective for public entities for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2016, including interim periods therein. Three basic transition methods are available &#x2013; full retrospective, retrospective with certain practical expedients, and a cumulative effect approach. Under the third alternative, an entity would apply the new revenue standard only to contracts that are incomplete under legacy U.S. GAAP at the date of initial application (e.g. January 1, 2017) and recognize the cumulative effect of the new standard as an adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings. That is, prior years would not be restated and additional disclosures would be required to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">72</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

		</p>

			<a href="#toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">enable users of the financial statements to understand the impact of adopting the new standard in the current year compared to prior years that are presented under legacy U.S. GAAP. Early adoption is prohibited under U.S. GAAP. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In August 2015, the FASB Issued ASU 2015-14 which deferred the effective date to December 31</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2017</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and the initial application date (e.g. January 1, 2018.) </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We do</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> not believe ASU 2014-09 will have a material effect on its financial statements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">In June 2015, the FASB issued ASU 2015-10,</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Technical Corrections and Improvements</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">(&#x201C;ASU 2015-10&#x201D;).</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">The amendments in ASU 2015-10&nbsp;affect a wide variety of Topics in the Codification and will apply to all reporting entities within the scope of the affected accounting guidance. ASU 2015-10&nbsp;includes amendments</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">to clarify the Codification,</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">correct unintended application of guidance, or make minor improvements to the Codification that are not expected to have a significant effect on current accounting practice or create a significant administrative cost to most entities. Additionally, some of the amendments will make the Codification easier to understand and easier to apply by eliminating inconsistencies, providing needed clarifications, and improving the presentation of guidance in the Codification.</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">The amendments in ASU 2015-10 are effective for financial statements issued for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2015, and interim periods within those fiscal years. Earlier adoption is permitted</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">, including adoption in an interim period. &nbsp;All other amendments in ASU 2015-10 are effective upon the issuance of ASU 2015-10.&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">The adoption of ASU 2015-10</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s financial condition and results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">In January 2016, the FASB issued </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">ASU 2016-01, &#x201C;Financial Instruments &#x2013; Overall (Topic 825-10): &#x201C;Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities.&#x201D; ASU 2016-01 amends the guidance on the classification and measurement of financial instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of the amendments in ASU 2016-01 include the following: 1) requires equity investments (except those accounted for under the equity method of accounting or those that result in consolidation of the investee) to be measured at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in net income; 2) simplifies the impairment assessment of equity investments without readily determinable fair values by requiring a qualitative assessment to identify impairment; 3) requires public business entities to use the exit price notion when measuring the fair value of financial instruments for disclosure purposes; and 4) requires an entity to present separately in other comprehensive income the portion of the total change in the fair value of a liability resulting from a change in the instrument-specific credit risk when the entity has elected to measure the liability at fair value; among others.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">ASU 2016-01 also </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">clarifies that an entity should assess the need for a valuation allowance on a deferred tax asset related to unrealized losses of investments in debt instruments recognized in OCI in combination with the entity&#x2019;s other defe</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">rred tax assets. Prior to this guidance</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">, the alternative approach used in practice evaluated the need for a valuation allowance for a deferred tax asset related to unrealized losses on debt instruments recognized in other comprehensive income separately from other deferred tax assets. This alternative approach will no longer be acceptable. </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">For public business entities, the amendments of ASU 2016-01 are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2017, including interim periods within those fiscal years.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not believe ASU 2016-01 will have a material effect on its financial statements.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In February 2016, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update No. 2016-02, &#x201C;Leases&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASU 2016-02&#x201D;). From the lessee's perspective, the new standard establishes a right-of-use (ROU) model that requires a lessee to record a ROU asset and a lease liability on the balance sheet for all leases with terms longer than 12 months. Leases will be classified as either finance or operating, with classification affecting the pattern of expense recognition in the income statement for a lessees. From the lessor's perspective, the new standard requires a lessor to classify leases as either sales-type, finance or operating. A lease will be treated as a sale if it transfers all of the risks and rewards, as well as control of the underlying asset, to the lessee. If risks and rewards are conveyed without the transfer of control, the lease is treated as a financing lease. If the lessor doesn&#x2019;t convey risks and rewards or control, an operating lease results.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2018, including interim periods within those fiscal years. A modified retrospective transition approach is required for lessees for capital and operating leases existing at, or entered into after, the beginning of the earliest comparative period presented in the financial statements, with certain practical expedients available. A modified retrospective transition approach is required for lessors for sales-type, direct financing, and operating leases existing at, or entered into after, the beginning of the earliest comparative period presented in the financial statements, with certain practical expedients available. We are currently evaluating the impact of the pending adoption of the new standard on its consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:18pt;"><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;"></font></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">73</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Federal Reserve Memorandum of Understanding</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In March&nbsp;2010, the Company agreed to enter into a written agreement (the &#x201C;Federal Reserve Agreement&#x201D;) with the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia (the &#x201C;Federal Reserve Bank&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In July&nbsp;2013, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System terminated the enforcement action under the Federal Reserve Agreement, and it was replaced with an informal non-public agreement, an MOU, with the Federal Reserve Bank, effective July&nbsp;17, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in this MOU are certain continued reporting requirements and a requirement that the Company receive the prior approval of the Federal Reserve Bank and the Director of Banking Supervision and Regulation of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System prior to declaring or paying any dividends on </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> capital stock, making interest payments related to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> outstanding trust preferred securities or subordinate securities, incurring or guaranteeing certain debt with an original maturity date greater than one year, and purchasing or redeeming any shares of stock. Please refer to &#x201C;Dividend and Interest Restrictions&#x201D; below for a discussion on the partial redemption of the Series A Preferred Stock. The MOU will remain in effect until stayed, modified, terminated or suspended in writing by the Federal Reserve Bank.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Dividend and Interest Restrictions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">On August&nbsp;13, 2009, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> Board suspended the regular quarterly cash dividends on the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">30,407</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares of Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and, accordingly, the Company is not permitted at this time to pay dividends on our Class A or Class B Common Stock. Additionally, under the terms of the Federal Reserve MOU, we are prohibited from redeeming the Series A Preferred Stock, or paying any dividends on shares of our stock without the prior written approval of the Reserve Bank and the Director of the Division of Banking Supervision and Regulation of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> received approval from the Federal Reserve Bank to bid up to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$14.0</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> million, which was raised in a private placement, to purchase shares of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock in an auction of such shares to be conducted by the </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">United States Department of Treasury (&#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Treasury&#x201D;).&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">On June 20, 2014, Treasury announced that it had priced auctions of preferred stock of </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">six</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> institutions, including all of the 30,407 shares of the Series A Preferred Stock, issued by the Company to the Treasury in 2009. The Series A Preferred Stock was priced in the auction at </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">$1,207.11</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> per share for all 30,407 shares of Series A Preferred Stock outstanding. As previously disclosed, the Company was a bidder in the auction and was allocated </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">11,551</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> shares of Series A Preferred Stock for repurchase at the clearing price of $1,207.11. Closing for the sale of the Series A Preferred Stock by Treasury, including the repurchase of 11,551 shares of Series A Preferred Stock by the Company, occurred on July 2, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The dividend in arrears </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">including interest </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">on the remaining 18,856 shares of Series A preferred stock is approximately </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">$8.</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">9</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> million.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In the event the Company declared the preferred dividend in arrears the Company&#x2019;s equity and capital ratios would be negatively affected; however, they would remain above the required minimum ratios.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Under the Federal Reserve MOU, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> may not declare or pay any dividends on </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> capital stock or make interest payments related to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> outstanding trust preferred securities or subordinate securities without the prior written approval of the Reserve Bank and the Director of the Division of Banking Supervision and Regulation of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. During the 201</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> received approval from the Federal Reserve Bank and paid all quarterly interest payments on the trust preferred securities.</font>
		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Mortgage-backed securities issued by U.S. government agencies and U.S. government sponsored enterprises:</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> As of December 31, 2015, we had three mortgage-backed securities with a fair value of $7.7 million and gross unrealized losses of $50 thousand.&nbsp;&nbsp;One of the mortgage-backed securities had been in an unrealized loss position for twelve months or longer. The unrealized loss is attributable to a combination of factors, including relative changes in interest rates since the time of purchase. The contractual cash flows for these securities are guaranteed by U.S. government agencies and U.S. government-sponsored enterprises. Based on its assessment of these factors, management believes that the unrealized losses on these debt securities are a function of changes in investment spreads and interest rate movements and not as a result of changes in credit quality.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management expects to recover the entire amortized cost basis of these securities. We do not intend to sell these securities before recovery of their cost basis and have not determined that it is not more likely than not that it will be required to sell these securities before recovery of their cost basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, management has determined that these securities are not other-than-temporarily impaired at December 31, 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">U.S. government issued or sponsored collateralized mortgage obligations (&#x201C;Agency CMOs&#x201D;):</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, we had 36 Agency CMOs with a fair value of $102.7 million and gross unrealized losses of $1.6 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Five of the Agency CMOs had been in an unrealized loss position for twelve months or longer and the other 31 Agency CMOs have been in an unrealized loss position for less than twelve months.&nbsp;&nbsp;The unrealized loss is attributable to a combination of factors, including relative changes in interest rates since the time of purchase.&nbsp;&nbsp;The contractual cash flows for these securities are guaranteed by U.S. government agencies and U.S. government-sponsored enterprises. Based on its assessment of these factors, management believes that the unrealized losses on these debt securities are a function of changes in investment spreads and interest rate movements and not as a result of changes in credit quality.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management expects to recover the entire amortized cost basis of these securities. We do not intend to sell these securities before recovery of their cost basis and have not determined that it is not more likely than not that it will be required to sell these securities before recovery of their cost basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, management has determined that these securities are not other-than-temporarily impaired at December 31, 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Non-agency collateralized mortgage obligations (&#x201C;Non-agency CMOs&#x201D;):</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, we had one non-agency CMO with a fair value of $1.1 million and a gross unrealized loss of $26 thousand.&nbsp;&nbsp;The bond has been in an unrealized loss position for less than twelve months.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not intend to sell this security before recovery of its cost basis, and it is not more likely than not we will be required to sell this security before recovery of its cost basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, management has determined that this security is not other-than-temporarily impaired at December 31, 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Municipal bonds:</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, we had s</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">even </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">municipal bonds with a fair value $6.1 million and gross unrealized losses of $52 thousand.&nbsp;&nbsp;All seven of the municipal bonds had been in an unrealized loss position for less than twelve months.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Because we do not intend to sell the bonds and it is not more likely than not that the we will be required to sell the bond before recovery of its amortized cost basis, which may be maturity, we do not consider the bonds to be other-than-temporarily impaired at December 31, 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Other securities:</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;As of December 31, 2015, we had </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">six</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> investments in private equity funds which were predominantly invested in real estate.&nbsp;&nbsp;In determining whether or not OTTI exists, we review the funds&#x2019; financials, asset values, and near-term projections.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2015, an OTTI charge of $14 thousand was recorded on one private equity investment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management concluded that the impairment on this investment was other-than-temporary.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 1pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We use a nine point grading risk classification system commonly used in the financial services industry as the credit quality indicator.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first four classifications are rated Pass.&nbsp;&nbsp;The riskier classifications include Pass-Watch, Special Mention, Substandard, Doubtful and Loss. The risk rating is related to the underlying credit quality and probability of default.&nbsp;&nbsp;These risk ratings are used in the calculation of the allowance for loan and lease losses.</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Pass: includes credits that demonstrate a low probability of default;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Pass-watch: a classification </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">which includes currently performing credits that are beginning to demonstrate above average risk through declining earnings, strained cash flows, increased leverage and/or weakening market fundamentals. This class may also include new loan originations which warrant approval but may contain certain risks that require closer than usual monitoring and supervision, such as construction loans;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Special mention: includes credits that have potential weaknesses that if left uncorrected could weaken the credit or result in inadequate protection of our position at some future date. While potentially weak, credits in this classification are marginally acceptable and loss of principal or interest is not anticipated;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Substandard accrual: includes credits that exhibit a well-defined weakness which currently jeopardizes the repayment of debt and liquidation of collateral even though they are currently performing. These credits are characterized by the distinct possibility that the Company may incur a loss in the future if these weaknesses are not corrected;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Non-accrual (substandard non-accrual, doubtful, loss): includes credits that demonstrate serious problems to the point that it is probable that interest and principal will not be collected according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">All loans are assigned an initial loan risk rating by the Chief Credit Officer (&#x201C;CCO&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The initial loan risk rating is approved by another member of executive management or by the appropriate loan committee approving the loan request. From time to time, and at the general direction of any of the various loan committees, the ratings may be changed based on the findings of that committee. Items considered in assigning ratings include the financial strength of the borrower and/or guarantors, the type of collateral, the collateral lien position, the type of loan and loan structure, any potential risk inherent in the specific loan type, higher than normal monitoring of the loan or any other factor deemed appropriate by any of the various committees for changing the rating of the loan. Any such change in rating is reflected in the minutes of that committee.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">NOTE 11.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> DERIVATIVE INSTRUMENTS AND HEDGING ACTIVITY</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2014, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> entered into a forward-starting interest rate swap agreement to hedg</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">e the risk of variability in our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> cash flows</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">attributable to changes in the 3 month LIBOR rate. This particular hedging objective was to reduce the intere</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">st rate risk associated with our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> forecasted issuances of 3 month fixed rate debt arising from a rollover strategy. This derivative was used as part of the asset/liability management process, is linked to a specific liability, and has a high correlation between the contract and the underlying item being hedged, both at inception and throughout the hedge period. The derivative was designated as cash flow hedge with the change in fair value recorded as an adjustment through other comprehensive income (loss) </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">until the underlying forecasted transactions occur, at which time the deferred gains and losses are recognized in earnings. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">As of December 31, 2015, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">an investment security</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> with a fair value of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">6</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">71</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> thousand</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;w</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">as</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> pledged as collateral to the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">counterparty of this transaction</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>

&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We are required to establish a valuation allowance for DTAs and record a charge to income or shareholders' equity if management determines, based on available evidence at the time the determination is made, that it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Management evaluates</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> the DTAs for recoverability using a consistent approach which considers the relative impact of negative and positive evidence, including historical profitability and projections of future reversals of temporary differences and future taxable income. </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">These estimates and judgments are inherently subjective.&nbsp; 			<font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:11pt;"><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Note 13.</font></font><font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:4pt;text-align:left"><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS WITH OFF-BALANCE-SHEET RISK AND CONCENTRATIONS OF </font><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">C</font><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">REDIT RISK</font></font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We are</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> a party to financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk in the normal course of business to</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> meet the financing needs of our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such financial instruments are recorded in the financial statements when they become payable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk in excess of the amount recognized in the consolidated balance sheets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The contract amounts of those instruments reflect the extent of involvement </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> ha</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ve</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> in particular classes of financial instruments.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is no violation of any condition established in the contract.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require payment of a fee.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since many of the commitments are expected to expire without being drawn upon, and others are for staged construction, the total commitment amounts do not necessarily represent immediate cash requirements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> evaluate each customer&#x2019;s creditworthiness on a case-by-case basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary by the Company upon extension of credit, is based on management&#x2019;s credit evaluation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Collateral held varies but may include personal or commercial real estate, accounts receivable, inventory or equipment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">us</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> to guarantee the performance of a customer to a third party.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those guarantees are primarily issued to support public and private borrowing arrangements, including commercial paper, bond financing and similar transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most guarantees extend for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">one year</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and expire in decreasing amounts through </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">October 201</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">6</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The credit risk involved in issuing letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved in extending loan facilities to customers.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> hold personal or commercial real estate, accounts receivable, inventory or equipment as collateral supporting those commitments for which collateral is deemed necessary.&nbsp;&nbsp;The extent of collateral held for those commitments is approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">75%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">NOTE 14. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">LEGAL CONTINGENCIES </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Royal Bank had a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">60%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> equity interest in each of CSC and RTL.&nbsp;&nbsp;CSC and RTL acquired, through public auction, delinquent tax liens in various jurisdictions thereby assuming a superior lien position to most other lien holders, including mortgage lien holders.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, the former President of CSC and RTL, CSC, RTL and the Company were named defendants, among others, in a Consolidated Master Class Action Complaint (the &#x201C;Complaint&#x201D;) filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey (&#x201C;Court&#x201D;) on behalf of a proposed class of taxpayers who became delinquent in paying their municipal tax obligations. The Complaint alleged a conspiracy to rig bids in municipal tax lien auctions.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">During 2013, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">the Company, Royal Bank, CSC, and RTL reached a settlement agreement with plaintiffs to settle the litigation for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$1.65</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> million and other terms and conditions, including an opportunity for members of the proposed settlement class whose tax liens are currently held by CSC or RTL to redeem those liens for a one-time cash payment equaling </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">85%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the redemption amount by making such payment within </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">35</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> days of the date of written notice. The proposed settlement class does not include, and therefore the offer to redeem does not apply to, tax liens acquired at </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">0%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> interest or at a premium.&nbsp;&nbsp;The settlement is subject to Court approval after notice and a hearing.&nbsp;&nbsp;Members of the proposed settlement class will have an opportunity to object to the proposed settlement or opt-out.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

Closing for the sale of the Series A Preferred Stock by the Treasury, including the repurchase of 11,551 shares of Series A Preferred Stock by the Company occurred, on July 2, 2014.</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> As part of this redemption, </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">we e</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">liminated nearly $3.5 million in preferred dividend in arrears.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> Class&nbsp;A common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Market under the symbol RBPAA.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is no market for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> Class&nbsp;B common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Class&nbsp;B shares may not be transferred in any manner except to the holder&#x2019;s immediate family.&nbsp;&nbsp;Class&nbsp;B shares may be converted to Class&nbsp;A shares at the rate of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1.15</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> to 1.&nbsp;&nbsp;Shareholders are entitled to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> vote for each Class&nbsp;A share and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ten</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> votes for each Class&nbsp;B share held.&nbsp;&nbsp;Holders of either class of common stock are entitled to conversion equivalent per share dividends when declared.</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Under the Pennsylvania Business Corporation Law, the Company may pay dividends only if it is solvent and would not be rendered insolvent by the dividend payment. There are also restrictions set forth in the Pennsylvania Banking Code of 1965 (the &#x201C;Code&#x201D;) and in the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (&#x201C;FDIA&#x201D;) affecting the payment of dividends to the Company by Royal Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the Code, no dividends may be paid by a bank except from &#x201C;accumulated net earnings&#x201D; (generally retained earnings).&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, dividends paid by Royal Bank to the Company would be prohibited if the effect thereof would cause Royal Bank&#x2019;s capital to be reduced below applicable minimum capital requirements.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2009, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> Board</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> suspended the regular quarterly cash dividends on the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> Board took this action in consultation with the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia as required by regulatory policy guidance.&nbsp;&nbsp;In February&nbsp;2014, the preferred cumulative dividend rate prospectively increased to 9%&nbsp;per annum.</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> As a result of </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times;font-size:10pt;">the Company&#x2019;s repurchase of 11,551 shares of Series A Preferred Stock, a</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">pproximately $3.5 million of the Series A Preferred stock</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">dividend in arrears was eliminated.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> As of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, the Series&nbsp;A Preferred stock dividend in arrears </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">including interest </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">was approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$8</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">9</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> million and has not been recognized in the consolidated financial statements.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">91</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 12pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In the event </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> declared the preferred dividend </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">in arrears our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> capital ratios would be negatively affected; however, they would remain above the required minimum ratios.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the Federal Reserve MOU as described in &#x201C;Note 2 &#x2014; Regulatory Matters and Significant Risks or Uncertainties&#x201D; to the Consolidated Financial Statements, the Company may not declare or pay any dividends without the prior written approval of the Reserve Bank and the Director of the Division of Banking Supervision and Regulation of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:11pt;"><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Note 16.</font></font><font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:4pt;text-align:left"><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Regulatory Capital Requirements</font></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company and Royal Bank are subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory and possible additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> assets, liabilities and certain off-balance-sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices. The Company&#x2019;s and Royal Bank&#x2019;s capital amounts and classification are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings and other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, the Company and Royal Bank met all capital adequacy requirements to which it is subject and Royal Bank met the criteria for a well-capitalized institution.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">In July 2013, the federal bank regulatory agencies adopted final rules to revise the agencies&#x2019; capital adequacy guidelines and prompt corrective action rules, which were designed to enhance such requirements and implement the revised standards of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, commonly referred to as Basel III. The July 2013 final rules generally implement higher minimum capital requirements, add a new common equity tier 1 capital requirement, and establish criteria that instruments must meet to be considered common equity tier 1 capital, additional tier 1 capital or tier 2 capital. The new minimum capital to risk-adjusted assets requirements are a common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5% (6.5% to be considered &#x201C;well capitalized&#x201D;) and a tier 1 capital ratio of 6.0%, increased from 4.0% (and increased from 6.0% to 8.0% to be considered &#x201C;well capitalized&#x201D;); the total capital ratio remains at 8.0% under the new rules (10.0% to be considered &#x201C;well capitalized&#x201D;).</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In connection with a prior bank regulatory examination, the FDIC concluded, based upon its interpretation of the Call Report instructions and under RAP, that income from Royal Bank&#x2019;s tax lien business should be recognized on a cash basis, not an accrual basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Royal Bank&#x2019;s current accrual method is in accordance with U.S. GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;Royal Bank disagrees with the FDIC&#x2019;s conclusion and filed the Call Report for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and the previous </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">21</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> quarters in accordance with U.S. GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;The change in the method of revenue recognition for the tax lien business for regulatory accounting purposes affects Royal Bank&#x2019;s and the Company&#x2019;s capital ratios as shown below.&nbsp;&nbsp;The resolution of this matter will be decided by additional joint regulatory agency guidance which includes the Federal Reserve Bank, the FDIC, and the OCC.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

The option price is equal to the fair market value at the date of the grant. The employee options are exercisable based on the grant&#x2019;s vesting schedule beginning </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> year after the date of grant and must be exercised within </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ten</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> years of the grant date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Directors&#x2019; options are exercisable on the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> year anniversary of the date of grant and must be exercised within </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ten</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> years of the grant date. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Compensation expense for stock options is recognized over the requisite service period. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">During </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">2014</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> recognized $</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">64</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> thousand</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$17 thousand</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively, in compensation expense for stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;A</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">t December 31, 2015, approximately</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">23</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> thousand</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> remained to be recognized in compensation expense over a weighted-average period of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">2.0</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> years.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Under the aforementioned LTI Plan, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we a</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">r</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">e</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> authorized to grant share-based incentive compensation awards for corporate performance to employees. These awards may be granted in </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">form of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">performace restricted </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">shares of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> common stock</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The vesting of awards is contingent upon meeting </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">performance</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> goals</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> stated in the specific awards when granted</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. The awards are not permitted to be transferred during the restricted time period from the date of the award and are subject to forfeiture to the extent that the performance restrictions are not satisfied. Awards are also forfeited if the employee terminates his or her service prior to the end of the restricted time period, unless such termination is in accordance with the Company&#x2019;s mandatory retirement age. Vested awards are converted to shares of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> common stock at the end of the restricted time period. The fair market value of each employee based award is estimated based on the fair market value of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> common stock on the date of the grant and probable performance goals to be achieved and estimated forfeitures. If such goals are not met then no compensation cost would be recognized and any recognized compensation cost would be reversed. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">At December 31, 2015 of the 703,131 shares available for future grants, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">225,000</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares are available for future restricted stock grants.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">During 2015, we recognized $</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">14</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> thousand in compensation expense for restricted stock grants.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">At December 31, 2015, approximately $</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">31</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> thousand remained to be recognized in compensation expense over a weighted-average period of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">2.0</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> years</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Note 19. Earnings Per Common Share</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> follow the provisions of FASB ASC Topic 260, &#x201C;Earnings per Share&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC Topic 260&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Basic earnings per share (&#x201C;EPS&#x201D;) excludes dilution and is computed by dividing income available to common shareholders by the weighted average common shares outstanding during the period.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> ha</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ve</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> classes of common stock currently outstanding. The classes are A and B, of which one share of Class&nbsp;B is convertible into </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.15</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares of Class&nbsp;A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Diluted EPS takes into account the potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised and converted into common stock using the treasury stock method. For </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">the years ended December 31, 2015 and 2014</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">96</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">655</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">170,239</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> options to purchase shares of common stock, respectively, were anti-dilutive in the computation of diluted EPS, as the exercise price exceeded average market price in each of those periods. Additionally warrants to purchase </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1,368,040</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares of Class A common stock were also anti-dilutive.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">FASB ASC Topic 220, &#x201C;Comprehensive Income&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC Topic 220&#x201D;), requires the reporting of all changes in equity during the reporting period except investments from and distributions to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">shareholders.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net income</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> is a component of comprehensive income (loss) with all other components referred to in the aggregate as other comprehensive income.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unrealized gains and losses on AFS securities is an example of another comprehensive income (loss) component.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Note 21.</font><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Under FASB ASC Topic 820 &#x201C;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC Topic 820&#x201D;), fair values are based on the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. When available, management uses quoted market prices to determine fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;If quoted prices are not available, fair value is based upon valuation techniques such as matrix pricing or other models that use, where possible, current market-based or independently sourced market parameters, such as interest rates. If observable market-based inputs are not available, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we use</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> unobservable inputs to determine appropriate valuation adjustments using discounted cash flow methodologies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Management uses its best judgment in estimating the fair value of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> financial instruments; however, there are inherent weaknesses in any estimation technique.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, for substantially all financial instruments, the fair value estimates herein are not necessarily indicative of the amounts </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> could have realized in a sales transaction on the dates indicated.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimated fair value amounts have been measured as of their respective period end and have not been re-evaluated or updated for purposes of these financial statements subsequent to those respective dates.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, the estimated fair values of these financial instruments subsequent to the respective reporting dates may be different than the amounts reported at each period-end.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ASC Topic 820 provides guidance for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">estimating fair value when the volume and level of activity for an asset or liability has significantly declined</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">identifying circumstances when a transaction is not orderly. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ASC Topic 820 establishes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to valuation methods used to measure fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level 3 measurements).&nbsp;&nbsp;The three levels of the fair value hierarchy under ASC Topic 820 are as follows:</font>
		</p>

		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

						<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Quoted prices in markets that are not active, or inputs that are observable either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the asset or liability. Valuation techniques include matrix pricing </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">which is a mathematical technique used widely in the industry to value debt securities without relying exclusively on quoted market prices for the specific securities but rather by relying on the securities&#x2019; relationship to other benchmark quoted prices.</font></p>

				</td>

						<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable (i.e., supported with little or no market activity).</font></p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">A financial instrument&#x2019;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> did not have transfers of financial instruments within the fair value hierarchy during </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">the years ended December 31, 2015 and 2014</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Items Measured on a Recurring Basis</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> available for sale investment securities are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Fair value for Level 1 securities are determined by obtaining quoted market prices on nationally recognized securities exchanges.&nbsp;&nbsp;Level 1 securities include common stocks.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Level 2 securities include obligations of U.S. government-sponsored agencies and debt securities with quoted prices, which are traded less frequently than exchange-traded instruments, whose value is determined using matrix pricing with inputs that are observable in the market or can be derived principally from or corroborated by observable market data.&nbsp;&nbsp;The prices were obtained from third party vendors.&nbsp;&nbsp;This category generally includes </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> mortgage-backed securities and CMOs issued by U.S. government and government-sponsored agencies, non-agency CMOs, and corporate and municipal bonds.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally,&nbsp;&nbsp;Level 2 includes derivative instruments whose valuations are based on observable market data.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Level 3 securities include investments in seven private equity funds which are predominantly invested in real estate.&nbsp;&nbsp;T</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">he value of the private equity funds are derived from the funds&#x2019; financials and K-1 filings.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> also review the funds&#x2019; asset values and its near-term projections.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">102</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Items Measured on a Nonrecurring Basis</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Non-accrual loans and TDRs are evaluated for impairment on an individual basis under FASB ASC Topic 310 &#x201C;Receivables&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;The impairment analysis includes current collateral values, known relevant factors that may affect loan collectability, and risks inherent in different kinds of lending.&nbsp;&nbsp;When the collateral value or discounted cash flows less costs to sell is less than the carrying value of the loan a specific reserve (valuation allowance) is established. OREO is carried at the lower of cost or fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is based upon independent market prices, appraised values of the collateral or management&#x2019;s estimation of the value of the real estate.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, for collateral acquired from tax liens, fair value may be established using brokers opinions due to their lower carrying value.&nbsp;&nbsp;These assets are included as Level 3 fair values, based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">For financial assets measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis, the fair value measurements by level within the fair value hierarchy used at </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> are as follows:</font>
