			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The following methods and assumptions were used to estimate the fair values of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> financial instruments at </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2014</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. The following information should not be interpreted as an estimate of the fair value of the entire Company since a fair value calculation is only provided for a limited portion of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to a wide range of valuation techniques and the degree of subjectivity used in making the estimates, comparisons between </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> disclosures and those of other companies may not be meaningful.&nbsp;&nbsp;The methodologies for estimating the fair value of financial instruments that are measured on a recurring or nonrecurring basis are discussed above.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Cash and cash equivalents (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The carrying amounts reported in the balance sheet for cash and short-term instruments approximate those assets&#x2019; fair values.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Securities:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Management uses quoted market prices to determine fair value of securities (level 1).&nbsp;&nbsp;If quoted prices are not available, fair value is based upon valuation techniques such as matrix pricing or other models that use, where possible, current market-based or independently sourced market parameters, such as interest rates (level 2). If observable market-based inputs are not available, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> use unobservable inputs to determine appropriate valuation adjustments by reviewing the private equities funds&#x2019; financials and K-1 filings (level 3).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Other Investment </font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">(carried at cost)</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">This investment includes the Solomon Hess SBA Loan Fund, which </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> inve</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">sted in to partially satisfy our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> community reinvestment requirement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Shares in this fund are not publicly traded and therefore have no readily determinable fair market value.&nbsp;&nbsp;An investor can have their investment in the Fund redeemed for the balance of their capital account at any quarter end with 60 days notice to the Fund.&nbsp;&nbsp;The investment in this Fund is recorded at cost.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> do not record this investment at fair value on a recurring basis, as this investment&#x2019;s carrying amount approximates fair value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Restricted investment in bank stock (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The carrying amount of restricted investment in bank stock approximates fair value, and considers the limited marketability of such securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">105</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Loans receivable (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The fair values of loans are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses, using market rates at the balance sheet date that reflect the credit and interest rate-risk inherent in the loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;Projected future cash flows are calculated based upon contractual maturity or call dates, projected repayments and prepayments of principal.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, for variable rate loans that re-price frequently and with no significant change in credit risk, fair values are based on carrying values.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Impaired loans (generally carried at fair value):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Impaired loans are accounted for under ASC Topic 310</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. Impaired</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> loans are those in which </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">we have</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> measured impairment generally based on the fair value of the loan&#x2019;s collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is generally determined based upon independent third-party appraisals of the properties, or discounted cash flows based on the expected proceeds.&nbsp;&nbsp;These assets are included as Level 3 fair values, based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Accrued interest receivable and payable (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The carrying amount of accrued interest receivable and accrued interest payable approximates its fair value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Deposit liabilities (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The fair values disclosed for demand deposits (e.g., interest and noninterest checking, passbook savings and money market accounts) are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (i.e., their carrying amounts).&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair values for fixed-rate certificates of deposit are estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that applies interest rates currently being offered in the market on certificates to a schedule of aggregated expected monthly maturities on time deposits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Short-term borrowings (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The carrying amounts of short-term borrowings approximate their fair values.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Long-term debt (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Fair values of FHLB advances and other long-term borrowings are estimated using discounted cash flow analysis, based on quoted prices for new FHLB advances with similar credit risk characteristics, terms and remaining maturity.&nbsp;&nbsp;These prices obtained from this active market represent a market value that is deemed to represent the transfer price if the liability were assumed by a third party.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Subordinated debt (carried at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Fair values of junior subordinated debt are estimated using discounted cash flow analysis, based on market rates currently offered on such debt with similar credit risk characteristics, terms and remaining maturity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Derivative instruments:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> ha</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ve</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> contracted with a third party vendor to provide</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> periodic valuations for our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> interest rate derivatives to</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> determine the fair value of our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> interest rate swaps. The vendor utilizes standard valuation methodologies applicable to interest rate derivatives such as discounted cash flow analysis and extensions of the Black-Scholes model. Such valuations are based upon readily observable market data and are therefore considered Level 2 valuations by the Company. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Off-balance sheet financial instruments (disclosed at cost):</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Fair values for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> off-balance sheet financial instruments (lending commitments and letters of credit) are based on fees currently charged in the market to enter into similar agreements, taking into account, the remaining terms of the agreements and the counterparties&#x2019; credit standing.&nbsp;&nbsp;They are not shown in the table because the amounts are immaterial.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">106</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Limitations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The fair value estimates are made at a discrete point in time based on relevant market information and information about the financial instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value estimates are based on judgments regarding future expected loss experience, current economic conditions, risk characteristics of various financial instruments, and other factors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">These estimates are subjective in nature and involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment and, therefore, cannot be determined with precision.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in assumptions could significantly affect the estimates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, the foregoing estimates may not reflect the actual amount that could be realized if all or substantially all of the financial instruments were offered for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;This is due to the fact that no market exists for a sizable portion of the loan, deposit and off balance sheet instruments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In addition, the fair value estimates are based on existing on-and-off balance sheet financial instruments without attempting to value anticipated future business and the value of assets and liabilities that are not considered financial instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other significant assets that are not considered financial assets include premises and equipment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the tax ramifications related to the realization of the unrealized gains and losses can have a significant effect on fair value estimates and have not been considered in any of the estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Finally, reasonable comparability between financial institutions may not be likely due to the wide range of permitted valuation techniques and numerous estimates which must be made given the absence of active secondary markets for many of the financial instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;This lack of uniform valuation methodologies introduces a greater degree of subjectivity to these estimated fair values.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Note 22. Related party transactions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">In the ordinary course of business, Royal Bank has had, and expects to have in the future</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> banking transactions with </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> officers, directors</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">and their affi</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">liates</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">which involve substantially the same terms as those prevailing at the time for comparable transactions with other parties not related to the bank</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">In the past we have originated loans to </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">related parties</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">. In accordance with Regulation O, related party loans were made on substantially the same terms, including interest rates and collateral, as those prevailing at the time for comparable transactions with unrelated persons and do not involve more than normal risk of collectability. The aggregate dollar amount of these loans and commitments was </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">$0</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> at December 31, 2015 and 2014. During 2015, there were no new related party loans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Related party deposits were </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">$12</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">6</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> million and </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">$</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">9</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> million at December 31, 2015 and 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:13pt;"><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Note 23</font><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">.</font></font><font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:4pt;text-align:left"><font style="display:inline;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:10pt;">Segment Information</font></font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">FASB ASC Topic 280, &#x201C;Segment Reporting&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC Topic 280&#x201D;) established standards for public business enterprises to report information about operating segments in their annual financial statements and requires that those enterprises report selected information about operating segments in subsequent interim financial reports issued to shareholders.&nbsp;&nbsp;It also established standards for related disclosure about products and services, geographic areas, and major customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating segments are components of an enterprise, which are evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision makers in deciding how to allocate and assess resources and performance.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> chief operating decision makers are the CEO and the CFO. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> We have</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> identified our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> reportable operating segments as &#x201C;Community Banking&#x201D; and &#x201C;Tax Liens&#x201D;.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 13.55pt;text-indent: -13.55pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Tax liens</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">At </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, Royal Bank&#x2019;s tax liens segment includes its </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">80%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">100%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> ownership interest in CSC and RTL, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to December 31, 2013, Royal Bank&#x2019;s ownership interest in </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">CSC</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and RTL was </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">60%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s tax liens segment consisted of purchasing delinquent tax certificates from local municipalities at auction and then processing those liens to either encourage the property holder to pay off the lien, or to foreclose and sell the property.&nbsp;&nbsp;The tax liens segment earns income based on interest rates (determined at auction) and penalties assigned by the municipality along with gains on sale of foreclosed properties. CSC is liquidating its assets under an orderly, long term plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;RTL ceased acquiring tax certificates at public auctions in 2010.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">ITEM 9A.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</font><a name="ITEM9ACONTROLSANDPROCEDURES_956475"></a>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">We</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> maintain a set of disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports filed under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#x201C;Exchange Act&#x201D;), is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#x2019;s rules and forms. As of the end of the period covered by this report, </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">we</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> evaluated, under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer (&#x201C;CEO&#x201D;) and Chief Financial Officer (&#x201C;CFO&#x201D;), the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures, as defined in Rule </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">13a-15(e) of the Exchange Act. </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">Based on that evaluation our CEO and CFO concluded that </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">There have been no changes in </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> internal control over financial reporting during the fourth quarter of </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">our </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">internal control over financial reporting. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">Our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Rule 13a-15(f) of the Exchange Act.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">Our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> manage</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">ment, with the participation of our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> principal executive officer and principal financial officer, has assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting base</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">d on the 2013</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> framework in </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">Internal Control-Integrated Framework</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (&#x201C;COSO&#x201D;).&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">Based on its assessment under the COSO fr</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">amework, </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> management concluded that the Company&#x2019;s control over financial reporting was effective as of </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">There are inherent limitations to the effectiveness of any controls system.&nbsp;&nbsp;A controls system, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that its objectives are met. Further, the design of a control system must reflect the fact that there are limits on resources, and the benefits of controls must be considered relative to their costs and their impact on the business model. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">This annual report does not include an attestation report of </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> registered accounting firm regarding internal control over financial reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#x2019;s report was not subject to attestation by </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> registered public accounting firm pursuant to the Dodd-Frank Act, which permits smaller reporting companies, such as the Company, to provide only management&#x2019;s report in this annual report.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
